analysis:
The supplied changes are the reconnect-timing refactor and its supporting types. ExponentialBackoff.nextDelay() becomes nextDelayRange(). It returns the equal-jitter range [det/2, det], and the caller is now expected to draw the random delay. CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift is new. It resets the backoff after a session open for at least 60 s. A coordinator close code 1012 gives a 0-1 s delay range without growing the backoff. All other ends take the next exponential range. CoordinatorSessionRecorder in CoordinatorClientState.swift is a lock-protected recorder of the open time and the coordinator close code. Tests are updated to match.

Security assessment, relevant to TB-002 and availability: the 1012 fast path lets the coordinator, which is trusted, steer the provider to reconnect within 0-1 s. A malicious coordinator-side attacker would first need to control the authenticated TLS channel, so this is not a provider-side regression. A fast reconnect after 1012 does not bypass registration, attestation or App Attest. Every reconnect still passes through the full register and authorization flow, and the provider's connection-scoped authorization is unaffected (T-053). The reset after 60 s stable sessions is bounded and cannot hold a connection open indefinitely without the peer's cooperation.

The diff does not touch the cryptographic, inference or cache paths (T-041, T-008) or the hold-socket path (TB-012). Edits in ProviderState are limited to header comments.

Not visible in supplied evidence: the CoordinatorClient call sites that consume nextDelayRange, draw the random delay, call markOpened and recordCloseCode, and call reset() after a clean end. Whether the actor correctly handles a ClosedRange of 0...0 or a degenerate range, and whether the recorder is created per attempt rather than shared across attempts, cannot be verified from this batch. The close code is 'coordinator side sent', so it is attacker-influenced only if the coordinator or the TLS channel is compromised. Integration should check that the call sites draw uniformly from the returned range and do not skip the delay on a 1012 loop, so that a coordinator repeatedly sending 1012 cannot produce a tight reconnect loop. The 0 s lower bound permits an immediate retry.
